summary.claimCountingMethod: Overlapping review units: 32 lesson claim groups, 112 formula blocks, 69 questions, six changed/requested alias entries (including two rejected), one new glossary definition.

corrections: Moved snd-waves-q8 from wave measurements to sample-phase increment so its sampled-sine and samples-per-cycle prerequisites precede it; original ID and key retained.
Added a local changing-frequency/absolute-time explanation and formula to wrapped-phase state before snd-waves-q11; its 44,880 Hz result independently recomputed.
Phase preservation avoids an output-value jump but does not guarantee no transient; abrupt slope changes and finite rounding now explained in lesson and questions.
Float headroom avoids clipping but is not lossless arithmetic; normal rounding still applies.
Full relative float precision restricted to the normal range; subnormal precision differs.
Digital full scale distinguished from the representable float range in dBFS prose, formula definition and question explanation.
TPDF output error has input-independent mean and variance; removed the stronger claim that every property of nonsubtractive total error is statistically independent.
Specified common TPDF dither as two quantisation steps peak-to-peak, including the moved dither question.
Distinguished formal SINAD-based ENOB from the question’s explicitly requested noise-only estimate from dynamic range; added verified SINAD glossary definition.
Separated BLIT impulse-train integration from BLEP/PolyBLEP step correction.
FM described as generating sidebands, which need not be harmonics.
Oversampling decimation filtering removes out-of-passband content; in-band aliases created at the oversampled rate survive.
High-rate hard-clipping experiment greatly reduces alias contamination; finite rate cannot remove the infinite harmonic tail.
Odd-only symmetric clipping statement restricted to a sine or other input with half-wave symmetry.
Added DC/Nyquist endpoint exceptions to the first FFT scaling description, and excluded these bins explicitly in the amplitude question.
Rectangular window allowed for coherent whole-cycle captures; removed universal “always window” instruction.
Added local zero-padding and scalloping/flat-top/interpolation context before FFT-bin and leakage questions.
DC question now specifies whole cycles of a steady waveform; lesson distinguishes partial-cycle mean from genuine DC offset.
Full-scale sample counts labelled as warnings for investigation, not proof that clipping happened, in WAV checklist and moved questions.
Eight-bit nearest-rounding question now explicitly excludes endpoint overload, retaining the same key.
Block-budget question now asks about meeting each block’s deadline, rather than an average which could conceal overruns.
Quantiser trace table reduced from five to four columns with all intermediate round/clip values retained.
Rejected new bare fixed-point alias because current hyphenated fallback could capture mathematical fixed points in other subjects; retained precise arithmetic aliases.
Rejected new bare phase alias because it would capture envelope “release phase” in another Synth module; used existing precise wave-phase phrase locally.
Fractional/negative powers no longer described as fractional numbers of repeated copies; roots and reciprocals made explicit.
Replaced obsolete original lesson-number cross-references with relevant short-unit names.
Hedged/removed: Phase jumps can cause clicks, rather than guaranteeing an output-value discontinuity in every specially timed case.
Hedged/removed: JND figures explicitly labelled secondary, condition-dependent examples; unsupported attentive-listener 5–6 cent claim removed.
Hedged/removed: Separated beat-envelope mathematics from fast-beat/roughness/two-tone perception; no universal audible-wobble boundary asserted.
Hedged/removed: Replaced broadly stated 100 extra x86 cycles with processor/instruction/mode-specific tens-or-hundreds wording and benchmarking advice.
Hedged/removed: Converter figures tied to typical A-weighted datasheet test conditions; removed blanket converter range/current flagship ranking.
Hedged/removed: Music crest factor 12–20 dB presented as an example, varying with programme and mastering.
Hedged/removed: Exact sampling reconstruction identified as ideal; real DAC finite filters, precision and analogue noise acknowledged.
Hedged/removed: Alias audibility made dependent on playback level and masking.
Hedged/removed: 12-TET described as a common default, removing unverified “almost all” coverage.
Hedged/removed: Removed unverified historical Moog popularisation attribution; retained its manufacturer-supported use of 1 V/oct.
Hedged/removed: Recorded violin note replaced with periodic sustained-tone approximation, with changing/noise components acknowledged.
Hedged/removed: RMS sine/square difference separated from precise perceived loudness, which also depends on spectrum and listening level.

Existing definition and original confidence retained unchanged as requested. Its SNR/dynamic-range shortcut describes noise-only resolution; formal ENOB uses SINAD. Active lesson/question explicitly distinguish this.

Existing definitions and confidences preserved. They simplify discontinuity and clipping conditions; active lessons now specify possible specially timed continuous phase changes and sample-peak versus reconstructed-peak limits.

lowConfidence.claim: Pitch discrimination thresholds and fast-beat perceptual boundaries
lowConfidence.reason: Research and UNSW demonstrations support dependence on stimulus/task/listener; no universal numerical threshold established. Lesson retains only explicitly hedged secondary examples.
C3 is inferred from the current manual’s full MIDI range C-2 to G8; future versions/products may use other octave labels.
Primary Intel documentation and older x86 measurements support variable penalties. No benchmark on the reader’s embedded target was performed; fixed-cycle claim removed.

lowConfidence.claim: Finished-board dynamic range and noise-only ENOB estimate
lowConfidence.reason: Chip figures verified with datasheet configurations and A-weighting; finished-board noise and SINAD were not measured. Dynamic-range substitution remains an explicitly approximate noise-only estimate.

lowConfidence.claim: AES17 convention and typical music crest-factor ranges
lowConfidence.reason: AES authoritative reference and indexed Audio Precision primary-manual excerpt support the conventions; full normative AES17 text not obtained. Music range is programme- and averaging-dependent and is hedged.

lowConfidence.reason: Confirmed in independent experiments with soundfile 0.14.0/libsndfile 1.2.2 and inspected versioned source. Behaviour can depend on library/platform/rounding configuration; text ties it to this runtime.

gaps: No original course topic removed: 68 original questions/keys, 51 original lesson equations, 20 Python lesson examples, three diagrams and two flow diagrams retained; one new sine question and one local glide formula added.

The 295 existing glossary definitions and confidence records are inherited from prior independent verification, not claimed as a fresh exhaustive definition audit. Real source limitations are retained; ENOB/JND/phase-jump/peak-level shorthand is explicitly flagged above.

Primary sources, formulas, all question keys/distractors and all code reviewed; claimsChecked counts 220 overlapping review units (32 lesson claim groups + 112 formula blocks + 69 question reviews + six requested alias-entry reviews + one new glossary definition), not 220 independently enumerated atomic claims.

Offline examples and exact outputs were tested, including PCM conversion boundaries. Hardware, audible quality, embedded callback timing, board noise and processor-specific slow paths were not measured.
BLIT/BLEP, oversampling filters and true-peak reconstruction are conceptual here; implementation depth remains in the later synthesis/audio-engineering modules.

Repository-wide formula/glossary scans also enumerate preserved archival files; their unchanged old lint forms are out of the active short-lesson editing scope. All active formula-lint hits are real inline program code permitted by Rule 6.
Complete app build, all-app tests and 390 px browser rendering are assigned to the coordinating session; this verifier does not modify generated data or shared compiler/app files.

AES Pro Audio Reference was fetched with the web browser for evidence, but the final Node accessibility check returned HTTP 403. Its newly added Further reading link was removed; evidence URL remains recorded as a browser-fetched source.

corrections: Bounded phase avoids growing-accumulator resolution loss but floating-point arithmetic still rounds.
The 100-cent equal-ratio semitone is explicitly 12-TET; other tunings have other semitone sizes and smaller intervals.
Wavetable is a general stored waveform; spectral restriction is deliberate, and interpolation/playback affect aliasing. Old Band-limited wavetable title retained as alias.

corrections: snd-waves.md: Bounded magnitude is not infinite arithmetic precision.
snd-waves.md: Phase continuity is not a guarantee of no audible transient.
snd-sampling.md: Distinguish toward-zero truncation from flooring and clipping.
snd-sampling.md: The displayed experiment violates the non-overload assumption at low bit depths.
snd-levels.md: Raw casts do not implement saturation.
snd-measuring.md: One-sided FFT scaling must not double unpaired endpoints.
snd-pitch.questions.json: Correct cents below A4; 98.7 is the interval above G4.
snd-waves.questions.json: Repeated blocks have spectral lines at block-rate harmonics, not original tone plus buzz.
snd-waves.questions.json: Avoid claiming phase continuity guarantees no audible transient.
snd-sampling.questions.json: Explain actual experiment, not just generic coarse quantisation.
snd-measuring.questions.json: Full-scale sample count is diagnostic, not definitive clipping detector.
snd-measuring.questions.json: Longer captures can remain halfway between bins.
snd-waves.md: Recursive oscillators and other designs need no explicit phase accumulator.
snd-aliasing.questions.json: Only out-of-passband harmonics are removed during decimation.
